_: The five findings of the red (Screening) hero, in the EXACT keys lot S1 declared (message of the night of 5 to 6). Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; S1 refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches that seal, and this file names each figure's cell in `source` beside it: {table, palier, seuil, mesure} reads releve[table].tables[palier][seuil][mesure] ({succes, n, taux, bas, haut}); {table, compte} reads releve[table][compte]. `source` is provenance for reviewers and future guards; builders may ignore it. Intervals in legends are Wilson 95% from the same cells, en dash, never an em dash. The rule behind finding 03 is the tool's own default (optimise: Wilson lower bound of recall >= 0.90, then the fewest false alerts), the same rule the live instrument applies: one rule on the whole site, chosen, not measured, and said on the fiche. `annotations` are fractions of the rendered tower box (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text), placed by the chef on the rendered states.

findings.titre: Exact matching raises no false alert, and finds few of the true matches.
findings.phrase: The tool keeps only the settings that catch at least 90% of true matches, then among those picks the one with the fewest false alerts. Exact matching catches 21.7% of them, and raises no false alert on the 60 pairs of near-matches, which are names that look similar but belong to different people. You use this to choose your own bar, on your own alerts.
findings.leg_a: recall, the share of true matches found: 21.7% on 60 pairs of confirmed matches, interval 13% to 34%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% on 60 pairs of near-matches, interval 0% to 6%
findings.rail: Exact matching catches 21.7% of true matches

findings.titre: Jaro-Winkler at 0.50 finds all 60 pairs of matches, and alerts on most near-matches.
findings.phrase: Jaro-Winkler is a score that says how similar two names look, from 0 to 1. If you set the bar at 0.50, the tool finds all 60 pairs of confirmed matches, and alerts on 85% of the 60 pairs of near-matches.
findings.leg_a: recall 100% for jaro-winkler at 0.50, interval 94% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 85% at the same cell, interval 74% to 92%, 60 pairs of near-matches
findings.rail: The lowest bar finds all 60 pairs of matches

findings.titre: Catching almost every true match costs a great many false alerts.
findings.phrase: This setting finds 98.3% of the true matches. It also alerts on 76.7% of the near-matches, because those pairs were written to be hard to tell apart. Run it on your alert history and the rate will be your own.
findings.leg_a: recall 98.3% for jaro-winkler at 0.56, interval 91% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 76.7% at the same cell, interval 65% to 86%, 60 pairs of near-matches
findings.rail: The setting the tool picks: 98.3% of matches found

findings.titre: The same setting alerts on 17.2% of generated pairs and 76.7% of the pairs we wrote.
findings.phrase: The same setting alerts on 76.7% of the 60 pairs of near-matches we wrote, and on 17.2% of the 360 pairs a script generated from them. A generated pair is easier to tell apart, so it is counted on its own, and the rates above come from the pairs we wrote.
findings.leg_a: false alerts 76.7% at the best cell on 60 pairs of near-matches we wrote, interval 65% to 86%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 17.2% at the same cell on 360 pairs of generated near-matches, interval 14% to 21%
findings.rail: Generated pairs are easier, so they are counted on their own

findings.titre: Run the same measurement on your own alert history.
findings.phrase: The rates here come from our public test set: 60 pairs of confirmed matches and 60 pairs of near-matches we wrote by hand, and another 360 pairs of each kind that a script generated. Run the tool on your own alert history and it writes the report into the folder your file is in.
findings.leg_a: 60 pairs of confirmed matches and 60 pairs of near-matches, written by us, behind the rates
findings.leg_b: another 360 pairs of each kind, generated by a script from the ones we wrote
